title: Complete DSA Roadmap for Campus Placements
summary: Step-by-step master guide from basic Arrays to Dynamic Programming and Graphs with targeted LeetCode problem recommendations.

sections.heading: Phase 1: Foundations (Week 1-3)
sections.content: Master time & space complexity Big-O notation. Solve 20 Easy problems on Arrays, Strings, Two Pointers, and Hash Maps.

sections.heading: Phase 2: Core Linear & Non-Linear (Week 4-6)
sections.content: Implement Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues, Binary Trees, and Binary Search Trees from scratch. Practice tree DFS/BFS traversals.

sections.heading: Phase 3: Advanced Optimization (Week 7-9)
sections.content: Master Graphs (BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, TopoSort) and Dynamic Programming (1D array optimization, 0/1 Knapsack, LIS, LCS).

title: System Design Primer for Undergraduates
summary: Clear, practical guide to scaling systems from 1 to 1,000,000 users: Load Balancers, Caching, Databases, and Microservices.

sections.heading: Horizontal vs Vertical Scaling
sections.content: Understand why horizontal scaling (scale-out) with stateless servers and distributed caches is the gold standard in tech.

sections.heading: Caching Strategies
sections.content: Explore Cache-Aside, Write-Through, and Write-Back policies using Redis to reduce database read latencies by 90%.

sections.heading: CAP Theorem Demystified
sections.content: Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance tradeoffs in modern distributed systems.

title: Google XYZ Resume Writing Playbook
summary: How to craft bullet points using the Google formula: 'Accomplished [X] as measured by [Y] by doing [Z]'.

sections.heading: The Google XYZ Formula
sections.content: Transform weak bullets into high-impact metrics. Instead of 'built a web app', write 'Engineered full-stack portal serving 1,200 active users with 99.4% uptime'.

sections.heading: Avoiding ATS Traps
sections.content: Do not use two-column tables, fancy icons, or images that confuse ATS PDF parsers. Stick to standard clean single-column hierarchy.

title: 30-Day Intensive Placement Sprint Plan
summary: Daily structured schedule balancing 2 DSA problems, 15 aptitude questions, and 1 mock interview session every day.

sections.heading: Daily Split (3 Hours/Day)
sections.content: 1.5 hours: 2 DSA problems. 45 mins: 1 timed aptitude test. 45 mins: Core CS revision (OS, DBMS, Networks).

sections.heading: Weekend Reviews
sections.content: Every Saturday: 1 full-length mock test. Every Sunday: Resume audit and 1 adaptive mock interview.
